text:
Maya Patel: Heads-up — I brought up paragon-embed-v0.3 (tiny) in staging and ran our standard onboard eval. Overall macro recall@10 is within 2% of prod, but recall@1 on short queries (<6 tokens) dropped ~6%. :thinking:
Liam Chen: huh, short queries only? that's interesting. any clustering/umap diffs?
Maya Patel: yes — ran UMAP on a 10k query sample, the short-query cluster is more diffuse vs prod. Uploaded snapshot to staging-artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood/paragon/umap-2026-03-20.png :eyes:
Nate Rivera: can you paste the eval command you used? I want to replicate locally.
Maya Patel: sure — eval-bot ran this: ```bash
python eval_embeddings.py --model paragon-embed-v0.3 --dataset shorttail-holdout --k 10 --metric recall@k --normalize True --quant none
```
Olivia Gomez: did you try disabling normalization? sometimes small models rely on length cues.
Maya Patel: tried normalize=False as well, recall@1 still down ~4%.
Sarah K: was this an int8 quant run or fp16? different kernel paths can change distances slightly.
Maya Patel: fp16 native run. we also tried an int8 ONNX export and that made recall@1 worse (drop ~9%).
Liam Chen: possible reasons: embedding distribution shift (centroid drift), different length scaling, different tokenization of short queries. did you check token counts/tokenizer differences vs prod model?
Maya Patel: tokenization is same vocab, but avg token counts identical. centroid mean moved ~0.08 L2 norm vs prod for short queries.
ate Rivera: (typo fix) Nate Rivera: i'll run a per-class centroid and nearest-centroid recall check. assign to me.
Nate Rivera: steps i'll run: 1) per-query-length recall@1/5/10 2) knn with cosine vs dot 3) re-normalize via mean-centering 4) cluster purity for short-query bucket
Olivia Gomez: also try kNN with higher ef/search params, to rule out ANN artifact. which index did you use?
Maya Patel: HNSW default ef=128 on staging, same as prod. I briefly increased to ef=512, no change.
Sarah K: screenshot of UMAP shows the short queries stretched along one axis — could be a single token embedding scale difference. check token embedding norms (embedding table L2 per token).
Maya Patel: good call — dumping token embedding norms now. eval-bot: token-norm-scan complete, top tokens with increased norms: ["_"] (stopwords), "api", "error" — short tokens look slightly higher by 10%.
Liam Chen: aha. that could skew short queries since they rely on 1-2 tokens. if token embeddings changed scale, whole sentence embedding shifts.
Nate Rivera: plan: re-run model with token-embedding layer LN fixed (freeze scale) and validate. if that helps, we can add a small post-normalization step: mean-center token-weighted embedding before pooling.
Maya Patel: quick patch test: ```python
def normalize_tokens(tokens, emb_table):
    vecs = emb_table[tokens]
    vecs = vecs - vecs.mean(axis=0)
    return vecs.mean(axis=0)
```
Maya Patel: running that now on sample.
(eval-bot): quick-scan results: mean-center pooling improves recall@1 on short queries from 44.2% -> 49.8% (prod baseline 50.6%). overall recall@10 unchanged. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Olivia Gomez: promising. if mean-centering fixes, we can make it a temporary postproc for paragon-v0.3 while we dig into token norm drift upstream.
Sarah K: let's also run contrastive calibration sweep (small LR on embedding table) to see if we can nudge norms without harming long queries.
Liam Chen: assign follow-ups: Nate to run full per-length grid + ANN params, Sarah to run small calibrations, Maya to open a rollout PR with optional mean-center flag and benchmark harness.
Maya Patel: opened PR https://github.com/redwood/paragon/pull/312 — flag `--postproc mean_center=True` added.
Nate Rivera: I'll post results by EOD. tagging @product if needed for risk decisions.
Maya Patel: thanks all. I'll add the UMAP + token-norm dump to the PR and attach the eval logs.
Olivia Gomez: good triage. if mean-centering is safe, we can canary it on 5% traffic in staging dedicated pool.
Maya Patel: noted. closing loop once Nate posts numbers. :white_check_mark:
